President Bola Tinubu has charged the Nigeria Police Force to respect citizens’ fundamental human rights and uphold professionalism, fairness and accountability in the discharge of their constitutional duties. He gave the charge on Saturday at the passing-out parade of the 8 Regular Cadets of the Nigeria Police Academy, Wudil, Kano State. The President was represented by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume. “As newly commissioned officers, I charge you to uphold the constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, respect for the fundamental rights of citizens and discharge your duties with professionalism, fairness and accountability. “Never allow the authority of your office to become an instrument of oppression, intimidation or personal enrichment. Be firm in enforcing the law, but always guided by justice, respect and respect for human dignity,” he urged. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources He said they must also recognise that public trust was one of the most valuable assets of any police institution, adding that their uniform represented more than authority. “It represents public trust, responsibility and a solemn obligation to respect every Nigerian irrespective of ethnicity, religion, political affiliation or social standing,” he said. According to him, public trust was earned through conduct, preserved through actions and strengthened through commitment to justice. He told the officers that they were no longer cadets in training but had stepped into a profession that demanded courage, integrity, discipline, selflessness and an abiding commitment to the service of humanity. One injured as fire guts Gombe residence AI-generated fake content threatens national security – Ex-FPRO IG appoints female AIG to oversee Bayelsa, Rivers The President said the Federal Government would continue to pursue reforms and provide the necessary support to strengthen the police’s capacity, improve personnel welfare and create an enabling environment for effective policing. He, however, said the success of those efforts would depend on their personal commitment to excellence, noting that the country expected much from them. Tinubu said their service would be measured not by the ranks they attained, but by the lives they protected, the communities they secured and the confidence they inspired in the people they served. In his address, the Commandant of the Academy, AIG Auwal Musa-Muhammad, described the day as one of celebrating discipline and readiness to make sacrifices for the nation. He said it marked the beginning of the officers’ journey in the service of the nation. The commandant “commended the Federal Government for the support it had given the academy, pointing out that it had encouraged the institution to pursue higher standards in its academic programmes and prepare the cadets to address the country’s security challenges.” The News Agency of Nigeria reports that 845 Assistant Superintendents of Police were commissioned, and awards were presented to some of them for their outstanding performances. ASP Benjamin John received the award for the most outstanding cadet of the academy, ASP Yakubu Abdullahi received the best drill award, while ASP Idris Muhammad received the award for best professional studies.
